legend: The thyroid parenchyma is affected by chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, in addition to showing a well-defined nodule of Langerhans cell histiocytosis (shown here). Epithelioid histiocytes with curved, bean-shaped nuclei are associated with numerous eosinophils (Fig. <<24003>>). The neoplastic cells are strongly and diffusely immunoreactive for S100 in the nucleus and cytoplasm (Fig. <<24005>>), and strongly and diffusely immunoreactive for CD1a (Fig. <<24006>>). There is CD207 (langerin) immunoexpression in the neoplastic cells adjacent to the thyroid follicles (Fig. <<25035>>).

diagnosis: Langerhans cell histiocytosis of the thyroid gland
legend: Langerhans cell histiocytosis involving the thyroid gland, comprising sheets of histiocytoid cells with vesicular nuclei that are often grooved, convoluted and indented, accompanied by pale to eosinophilic cytoplasm. Residual thyroid follicles with luminal colloid are seen among the sheets of histiocytoid cells which have infiltrated into surrounding tissue including skeletal muscle fibres. Eosinophils and scattered small lymphocytic aggregates are also observed.
